name: Quick Refrigerator Pickles
why: You asked about pickling and you already own everything. No canning, no boiling jars, no risk. These live in the fridge and you eat them within a month.

ingredients.display: black peppercorns, or 1/2 tsp ground pepper

steps.text: Wash 2 jars in hot soapy water and rinse. That is the whole sterilising step.
steps.look: These are refrigerator pickles, not canned ones. They are never sealed and never stored at room temperature, so the boiling-water canning process that makes preserving intimidating simply does not apply.
steps.warn: The flip side of that: these must live in the fridge from the moment they are made, and they keep about a month. They are not shelf stable and must never be treated as if they are.

steps.text: Slice the cucumbers into rounds about 5 mm thick, or into spears if you prefer.
steps.look: Five millimetres is about the thickness of two stacked coins. Thinner slices go limp, thicker ones stay crunchy but take longer to taste of anything. Your multi-blade slicer does this in seconds and more evenly than a knife.

steps.text: Peel 3 garlic cloves and crush each one flat under the side of your knife.
steps.look: Lay the flat of the blade over the clove and press down with your palm until it cracks. The skin then slips off on its own. Crushed rather than chopped: you want the flavour, not garlic pieces in every mouthful.

steps.text: Put 1 cup vinegar, 1 cup water, 1 tbsp kosher salt and 1 tbsp sugar in a small pot. Heat on medium, stirring, just until the salt and sugar dissolve. Do not boil.
steps.look: This is the brine. It will look cloudy at first and go clear once everything dissolves, which takes about 2 minutes. That clearing is the signal, not the temperature.The sugar is not there to make them sweet, it balances the sharpness of the vinegar. A tablespoon across two jars is not enough to taste as sweetness.

steps.text: Pack the cucumber slices into the jars with the garlic, peppercorns and the crushed red pepper if using. Pack them in tightly.
steps.look: Tight packing keeps the slices under the brine. Anything floating above the liquid does not pickle and will spoil first.

steps.text: Pour the warm brine over until everything is completely covered. Let it cool on the counter for about 30 minutes, then lid it and refrigerate.
steps.look: Cooling before the lid goes on stops condensation collecting under the lid.

steps.text: Wait 24 hours before eating. Best after 3 days. Keeps about a month in the fridge.
steps.look: They are edible after a few hours but taste like cucumber in vinegar. The flavour needs a day to get into the middle of each slice.Zero protein. This is a crunchy, sharp thing to put next to rich food, and it turns two cucumbers that would otherwise go soft into something that lasts a month.
